newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks lower, market seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks lower, market seen stabilising.

text.p: Croatian stocks nudged lower in modest buying on Tuesday with further dips across the board for issues that rose steeply over the past month.
But the market was seen as stabilising after declining on disturbing news about tighter regulations for foreign investors in neighbouring Slovenia and renewed ethnic conflicts in Mostar, Bosnia.
"Things were saved by (drugs firm) Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka, especially after they recovered in London," said Hrvoje Poljak, analyst at I.F.C. consultancy and brokerage.
The two market heavyweights, closing at 490 and 1,860 kuna respectively, regained most of the ground they had lost in a general drop last week.
Losers beat gainers seven to four on Tuesday and one of 12 traded issues closed flat. Volume dipped to 12,832 units and turnover to 7.1 from last Friday's 18.3 million kuna.
"We were not very active today," said one trader with a large market share.
Food stocks Podravka was the most actively traded, losing two kuna to close at 318 with 3,878 units sold.
Poljak said that may have been the lowest level and after touching it, Podravka was almost certain to rebound.
He also pointed out a renewed buying interest in chocolate maker Kras that may help it post further gains in coming days.
"Rather than the whole market, investors are now targeting a few selected issues. Apart from Pliva and Zagrebacka, I think these are definitely Podravka and Kras," he added.
Kras added five kuna to close at 480 on volume of 1,939.
The day's biggest loser was Adriatic pipeline operator Janaf, down 1,900 kuna to 7,000 with only eight shares sold. It was pencilled in for partial privatisation later this year.
Most hoteliers were also among decliners, but Istraturist and Suncani Hvar bucked the trend.
Istraturist was top gainer, adding 15 kuna or 7.89 percent to 205 kuna on volume of 338 units.
Dalmatian hotels Suncani Hvar ended one kuna firmer at 65 after 1,222 shares were traded in a 65-71 kuna range.
